meta.baslik: AI traces: writing rules and checker
meta.aciklama: A 159 item rule set for removing known AI writing habits from academic texts, and a trace checker that runs in your browser. Free, no sign-in; your text never leaves your device.

baslik: Remove AI traces from your text
giris: This page has two things: a writing rule set you can give to an AI assistant, and a trace checker that scans your text in your browser. Both are free and need no sign-in.
amac: The aim is not to fool a detector. It is to remove the known bad writing habits of AI from the text and to keep the grounds of every claim. If your institution or journal asks you to disclose AI use, you disclose it.

yazma.metin: For a thesis or article template, a check of your Word file and a writing coach, go to the Writing page.

istem.baslik: Copy the prompt with one click
istem.aciklama: The whole rule set is ready as a single prompt. Copy it and paste it into the AI assistant you use. Before taking your text, the assistant asks you eight questions and works according to your answers.
istem.kopyalandi: The prompt was copied to the clipboard.
istem.kopyalanamadi: The clipboard is not available. The whole prompt is selected below; copy it with Ctrl+C (Cmd+C on Mac).
istem.yedekIpucu: The text is selected. Press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C to copy it.

denetleyici.baslik: Check your text in the browser
denetleyici.aciklama: Paste your text. Word and phrase lists, chat leftovers, citation traces, dashes, placeholders and sentence rhythm are marked with the rule number.

gizlilik.baslik: Your text does not leave your device
gizlilik.metin: The check runs on this page, inside your browser. The text you paste is not sent to any server or AI provider, and it is not stored or logged. When you close the page, the text is gone.

uyari.baslik: This is not an AI detector
uyari.metin: The result does not pass judgement on who wrote the text. It only shows the number and density of traces from the rule set. False positives happen: people writing in a second language, formulaic official style and short texts are often flagged wrongly. A single trace is not proof; the strong signal is several kinds of traces clustering in the same text (rules 9.3, 9.4, 9.5).

alan.ipucu: At most {sinir} characters. Headings and paragraphs are separated by line breaks.

hata.bos: Paste a text to check first.
hata.uzun: The text can have at most {sinir} characters; it has {sayi} now.

durum.yok: Check finished. None of the listed patterns was found. This does not show that the text follows the rule set; it only says that the traces this checker measures were not seen.
durum.temizlendi: The text and the results were cleared.

sonuc.aciklama: Certain trace: a leftover that should never be in the text (chat sentence, citation trace, placeholder, Markdown remnant). Probable trace: a pattern named in the rule set. Weak trace: a word that is no problem alone and only matters when it piles up. Visible marker: a mark the author placed on purpose, such as [KAYNAK GEREKLİ]; it is not counted as a trace.

ritim.not: These figures are not a detector score; they only indicate monotony (rule 10.6).

olcum.degiskenlik: Sentence length looks monotonous (coefficient of variation {deger}). The 0.30 threshold is a heuristic; the rule text has no numeric threshold.
olcum.mektedirDir: {deger}% of the sentences end in -mektedir or -dır. The rule limits this to half of a paragraph.
olcum.tirnak: Straight quotes (") and curly quotes (“ ”) are mixed. Pick one.
olcum.kesme: Straight apostrophes (') and curly apostrophes (’) are mixed. Pick one.
olcum.kisaMetin: The text has only {deger} words. Figures are unreliable for short texts; the chance of a false positive is high.

tekrar.not: The most frequent connectors and stock verbs in the text. Counting does not replace reading (rule 10.4).

isaretli.aciklama: The line style shows severity: solid thick line is certain, dashed is probable, dotted is a weak trace. See the findings list for details.

kurallar.aciklama: The readable form of the prompt. Each item is cited as section.item; the findings of the checker link to these numbers. The second list of section 9 is numbered 9.7 to 9.12, because in the source text the numbering starts again from 1. The rule text itself is Turkish.
